claims: Trump Accounts (530A accounts) are tax-advantaged investment accounts for children under 18.
Trump Accounts (530A accounts) offer a federal $1,000 "seed" contribution for children born between 2025 and 2028.
Parents can open Trump Accounts (530A accounts) to invest up to $5,000 annually in US stock index funds.
Funds in Trump Accounts (530A accounts) are tax-deferred until age 18.
Children born between Jan 1, 2025, and Dec 31, 2028, qualify for an initial $1,000 from the government, notes WHYY and this YouTube video.
Families can contribute up to $5,000 annually per child, notes ERS Texas (.gov) and this YouTube video.
Parents can file IRS Form 4547 during the 2026 tax season for children born in 2025.
Funds in Trump Accounts (530A accounts) are locked until the child turns 18, notes the National Association of REALTORS® and this YouTube video.
Funds in Trump Accounts (530A accounts) are intended for expenses such as higher education or a first-time home purchase, notes the National Association of REALTORS® and this YouTube video.
Trump Accounts (530A accounts) can be requested via tax forms.
An official enrollment portal is set to launch in summer 2026, says the National Association of REALTORS® and this YouTube video.
Trump Accounts (530A accounts) are designed to operate similarly to IRAs.
Trump Accounts (530A accounts) must be invested in low-cost US stock index mutual funds or ETFs, according to ERS Texas (.gov) and this YouTube video.
